How the models are built

Every method below is tied to a project where it was actually used.

Method areas

Seven method areas, each with the projects where it was used.

  1. Mechanistic and eco-evolutionary modelling

    Models built from explicit processes rather than fitted curves: immigration, interaction, diversification and extinction as rates; traits under selection; populations whose dynamics feed back on evolution. Ecological and evolutionary change are treated on the same timescale where the question demands it.

    Used inThe evolutionary consequences of isolation (PhD) · Trait evolution in mutualistic networks (supervised MSc)

  2. Stochastic simulation and numerical experiments

    Individual- and population-level stochastic models studied by simulation when analytical solutions are out of reach. Simulation engines are written in C++ for speed; experiments are designed, run and analysed from R.

    Used inThe evolutionary consequences of isolation (PhD) · Regime shifts in Mediterranean communities (MSc)

  3. Dynamical systems, transitions and resilience

    Equilibria, stability and abrupt transitions. Catastrophe theory for discontinuous community dynamics, and regime-shift analysis of community time series under multiple pressures.

    Used inRegime shifts in Mediterranean communities (MSc)

  4. Interaction networks and systems frameworks

    Interactions represented explicitly as networks whose structure depends on traits and feeds back on dynamics; the same systems view applied to organisations and institutions.

    Used inTrait evolution in mutualistic networks (supervised MSc) · Organisations, institutions and sustainability

  5. Trait space, functional diversity and phylogenetics

    n-dimensional hypervolumes to quantify occupied trait space; phylogenetic inference and phylogeny-informed trait imputation to handle incomplete trait data.

    Used inFunctional diversity of Mediterranean fish communities

  6. Statistical analysis and model-to-data comparison

    Estimating the effects of pressures from observational data, comparing model expectations with community records, and quantitative analysis of survey and monitoring data.

    Used inRegime shifts in Mediterranean communities (MSc) · Tracking marine invasions with citizen science · Organisations, institutions and sustainability

  7. Spatial analysis, oceanographic models and visualisation

    GIS analysis (QGIS, ArcGIS), satellite imagery, and a year of operational work with oceanographic models and forecasts. Data visualisation and scientific storytelling for climate-change reporting.

    Used inHydrographic Service, Hellenic Navy (2024–2025) · Political Economy of Sustainable Development Lab
